skills.title: Audit and remediate question sets without breaking semantic or release contracts
skills.content:
- Calculate baseline membership and counts from the current manifest and data at run time; prose counts are descriptive and may be stale.
- Determine word-versus-idiom status from an explicit per-question contract or authoritative metadata. Do not infer it solely from whitespace because multi-word modals and other lexical units are not necessarily idioms.
- Before changing builders or generated data to satisfy structural checks, complete the content, distractor, and answer-uniqueness review. Structural conformity must not certify semantic quality.
- Preserve stable question identity and stored q-based progress when moving idiom questions into a contiguous range. If reordering is unavoidable, document the compatibility impact and migration or reset policy before implementation.
- Define how multi-word modal expressions are represented. If they remain word items, document IPA as optional or an accepted warning; otherwise provide a deliberate alternate representation instead of silently suppressing warnings.
- Separate audit, report, plan, implementation, and deploy write sets. In a dirty worktree, record the pre-existing diff and stage only the intended release files.
- Use a closed verification chain after remediation: regenerate from builders, run set-specific checkers, run check_q1_data, run npm test, rerun the scoped structural audit to ERROR 0, then verify the deployment run and published content-bearing JSON when release is requested.
